query: Isolation of mouse skeletal muscle satellite cells by enzymatic digestion and fluorescence-activated cell sorting
title: Protocol for the isolation of mouse muscle stem cells using fluorescence-activated cell sorting
markdown:
## Protocol: Isolation of mouse skeletal muscle satellite cells by enzymatic digestion and fluorescence-activated cell sorting

### Overview

This protocol details the isolation of mouse skeletal muscle satellite cells (MuSCs) via enzymatic digestion and mechanical dissociation, followed by fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS). The process includes preparation of reagents, tissue extraction, multi-step enzymatic digestion to release MuSCs from myofibers, antibody staining for surface markers, FACS purification based on specific antigen profiles (CD45-, CD11b-, TER119-, SCA1-, CD31-, β1 Integrin+, CXCR4+), and subsequent culture or transplantation procedures.

### Materials/Reagents

DMEM, Collagenase Type II (285 U/mg), F10 medium, Fetal Bovine Serum (FBS) or Donor Bovine Serum (DBS), Hank's Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS), Propidium Iodine (PI), Calcein Blue (CB), APC-conjugated antibodies, APC-Cy7-conjugated antibodies, PE-Cy7-conjugated antibodies, Streptavidin-PE-Cy7, PBS, EDTA (5 mM), Paraformaldehyde (PFA), Triton-X, Normal Goat Serum, BSA, Hoechst stain, Growth Media (GM), Differentiation Media (DM), bFGF, TRIzol LS, Lentivirus, Polybrene, Cardiotoxin (CTX) or Barium Chloride (BaCl2), Saline.

### Equipment

BD FACS Aria III cytometer (70 µm nozzle), 5 mL FACS tubes, 50 mL conical tubes, 15 mL conical tubes, 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes, Petri dishes, Glass Pasteur pipets with latex bulbs, Serological pipettes (various sizes), P200 pipette, 31-gauge insulin syringe, 40 µm and 70 µm cell strainers, Shaking water bath (55 RPM), Centrifuge, Hemocytometer, Microscope, Biosafety cabinet (Class II).

### Safety & Sterility

Euthanize mice according to institutional IACUC protocol. Maintain sterile technique throughout dissection and cell processing. Use 70% ethanol to disinfect work surfaces and tools between samples to prevent cross-contamination. Handle lentivirus in a Biohazard Class II biosafety cabinet. Dispose of sharps in appropriate bins. Wear appropriate personal protective equipment when handling chemicals such as cardiotoxin, barium chloride, and TRIzol LS.

## Reagent Preparation

### Preparation Phase

1. Prepare Digest 1 Mix by adding 0.2% Collagenase Type II to DMEM. Keep the solution on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Prepare Digest 1 Stop Solution by adding 20% FBS or DBS to F10 medium. Keep the solution on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. Prepare Staining Media (SM) by adding 2% FBS or DBS to HBSS. Keep the solution on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->

## Antibody Staining

### 2-2.5 h [branch: Antibody staining of mono-nuclear cells associated with skeletal muscle]

1. Label 5 mL FACS tubes for unstained controls, single-color controls (SSC), and fluorescence-minus-one (FMO) controls as follows: a. Unstained; b. SSC-Propidium Iodine (PI); c. SSC-Calcein Blue (CB); d. SSC-APC; e. SSC-APC-Cy7; f. SSC-PE-Cy7; g. FMO-APC; h. FMO-APC-Cy7; i. FMO-PE-Cy7. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S113 -->
2. Label FACS tubes for each experimental sample. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S114 -->
3. Transfer 4×10^6 cells into their respective FACS tubes in a final volume of 400 µL of SM. CRITICAL: Maintain a ratio of 1×10^6 cells per 100 µL of SM, as antibodies have been titrated to work optimally at this concentration. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S115 -->
4. Stain cells in control and experimental samples with fluorescently conjugated antibodies according to the specified staining scheme to detect target antigens (Table 1). Shield stained cells from light and keep tubes partially immersed in ice to prevent internalization of antibodies. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S04 -->
5. Incubate stained cells on ice for 30 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S05 -->
6. Wash stained cells by adding 3 mL of SM to each FACS tube. Centrifuge at 360 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C. Decant the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 400 µL of SM. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S06 -->
7. Incubate stained cells with PE-Cy7 Streptavidin antibody for 20 minutes while keeping them on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S07 -->
8. Wash stained cells by adding 3 mL of SM to each tube. Centrifuge at 360 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C. Remove the supernatant and repeat the wash step one additional time, for a total of two washes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S08 -->
9. Filter cells through a 40 µm cell strainer into freshly labeled FACS tubes to prepare for FACS analysis. Keep stained cells in tubes immersed on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S09 -->

### 15 min prior to FACS

1. Add PI and Calcein Blue to corresponding tubes 15 minutes prior to FACS analysis (Table 1). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S01 -->

## FACS Purification

### 2-4 h

1. Set up the BD FACS Aria III cytometer as specified by the manufacturer. Use a 70 µm nozzle with a flow rate of 2.0–4.0. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S116 -->
2. Run the unstained control to set the background voltage for each channel. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
3. Run each single-color control (SCC) sample to set the voltage for positive cells. Record events for the top 25% of expressing events for fluorophore compensation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->
4. After compensating for all channels, run FMO samples to assist with drawing negative gates for APC (CD45, CD11b, TER119, SCA1, CD31) and positive gates for APC-Cy7 (β1 Integrin) and PE-Cy7 (CXCR4) (Figure 5). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->
5. Sort CD45-; CD11b-; TER119-; SCA1-; CD31-; β1 Integrin+; CXCR4+ MuSCs for further analysis. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S05 -->

### ﬁrst 48 hours

> **Operational constraint:** Do not remove media completely within the first few days after FACS isolation, as MuSCs have low adherence during the first 48 hours. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S117 -->

## Procedure

### Prepared 24 h prior to the procedure

1. Pre-coat wells of a multi-well culture plate with enough Coating Media to cover the entire bottom of the well. Incubate the plates for 24 hours at 37°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->

### Preparation of muscle digestion media

1. Prepare Digest 1 mix containing 0.2% Collagenase Type II (285 U/mg) dissolved in DMEM. Pass the digest 1 solution through a filtered tissue culture bottle (Thermo Scientific, Cat# 1570020) and keep on ice until step 8. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->

### Extraction of mice skeletal muscle

1. Prepare a decontaminated dissection field on a benchtop by cleaning it with 70% ethanol. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S01 -->
2. Transfer 20 mL of Digest 1 mix into a tube labeled 'Digest 1'. Prepare one tube for each replicate mouse. Keep the tubes on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S02 -->
3. Euthanize mice according to your institution's approved IACUC protocol. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S03 -->
4. Spray down the mouse with 70% ethanol, remove the skin, and extract hindlimb, triceps, and abdominal skeletal muscles. Place the extracted muscles into the tube containing ice-cold Digest 1 mix. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S04 -->
5. Seal the tube containing Digest 1 and muscle with parafilm. Keep the tube on ice until step 8. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S05 -->
6. Repeat steps 4–6 for each additional replicate mouse. Disinfect dissection tools and the dissection platform between each mouse with 70% ethanol to avoid cross-contamination of samples. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S06 -->

### Enzymatic and mechanical dissociation

1. Disinfect tubes with 70% ethanol and incubate tube(s) containing Digest 1 and muscle at 37°C in a shaking (55 RPM) water bath for 90 minutes. Use weighted rings to keep 50 mL conical tubes secured to the bottom of the shaking bath. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S01 -->
2. During Digest 1 incubation, prepare the following: a. Prepare glass tips (1 per mouse) for trituration by safely breaking off the thin barrel of a glass Pasteur pipet and attaching a latex bulb over the broken opening. b. Label three 50 mL conical tubes per mouse. c. Prepare 5 mL of Digest 1 stop solution (20% FBS or DBS in F10) for each mouse. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S02 -->
3. After Digest 1 incubation is complete, remove floating debris from Digest 1 tubes by carefully decanting each tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S03 -->
4. Inactivate Digest 1 by adding 5 mL of Digest 1 stop solution to each tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S04 -->
5. Gently swirl the tube(s) to mix. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S05 -->
6. Carefully add 25 mL of PBS to each Digest 1 tube by pipetting to the wall of the tube. Slowly decant the supernatant, leaving only a small amount of liquid covering the muscle. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S06 -->
7. Repeat Step 13 two more times to remove residual Digest 1 Mix. The supernatant should become clearer with each wash. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S07 -->
8. After the third wash, pour all muscles into a petri dish that contains 25 mL of PBS to start the trituration process. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S08 -->
9. Gently triturate the largest muscles (i.e., quadriceps and gastrocnemius) first, mincing several times for each muscle. During the first round of trituration, the PBS solution should turn very cloudy from myofibers released into solution. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S09 -->
10. Collect all the solution (including released myofibers which contain MuSCs under their basal lamina) from the petri dish using a serological pipette. Split the collected solution equally into two 50 mL collection tubes for each mouse. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S10 -->
11. Add 25 mL of PBS into the petri dish for a second round of mincing. Triturate smaller muscles (i.e., triceps, tibialis anterior, and abdominal muscles). Repeat Step 16. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S11 -->
12. Add 25 mL of PBS into each dish for a third round of mincing. Triturate all muscles. Repeat Step 16. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S12 -->
13. Fill up each sedimentation collection tube to 50 mL with PBS. Place all tubes upright in a stationary 37°C incubator for 25 minutes for gravitational sedimentation to occur. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S13 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: The sedimentation step separates interstitial cells (low density) from myofibers (high density). Tubes should be minimally perturbed through steps 19–26. Rough handling at this stage will lead to myofibers being resuspended in the supernatant, which will decrease the final MuSC yield. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S14 -->
14. During the first sedimentation step, label one 50 mL conical tube per mouse and keep the tube on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S15 -->
15. Collect the interstitial cells (ICs) (i.e., supernatant in collection tubes), including MuSCs liberated early from myofibers after Digest 1, and use them for single-color and fluorescence-minus-one (FMO) controls. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S16 -->
16. After the first sedimentation step is complete, carefully remove the collection tubes from the incubator. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S17 -->
17. a. Collect 15 mL of supernatant from each tube and deposit the solution into the ICs tube(s) and leave on ice. b. Subsequently, add 15 mL of fresh PBS to each sedimentation tube by pipetting onto the side of the wall for each tube. Be careful not to disturb the myofiber sediment at the bottom of the tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S18 -->
18. Incubate the collection tubes for 15 minutes at 37°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S19 -->
19. During the second sedimentation step, prepare Digest 2 mix (0.0125% Collagenase Type II (285 U/mg)/0.05% Dispase II (1.81 U/mg) in F10). Keep Digest 2 mix at 37°C until needed in step 27. Filter Digest 2 mix through a filtered tissue culture bottle (Thermo Scientific, Cat# 157-0020). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S20 -->
20. Carefully remove 20 mL of supernatant from each sedimentation tube. Gently add 20 mL of fresh PBS into the tube without disturbing sediment at the bottom of the tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S21 -->
21. Incubate the sedimentation tubes for 10 minutes at 37°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S22 -->
22. Gently remove supernatant to the 15 mL mark for each tube and immediately add 15 mL of prewarmed Digest 2 mix to each tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S23 -->
23. Seal each tube with parafilm and incubate tubes at 37°C in a shaking (55 RPM) water bath for 30 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S24 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: Do not digest myofibers for longer than 30 minutes. Over-digestion leads to excessive cleavage of cell surface markers that are necessary for FACS-based isolation of MuSCs. Thus, longer times in Digest 2 may decrease MuSC yield during FACS-isolation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S25 -->

### After 30 min

1. After 30 minutes, immediately inactivate Digest II by adding 2 mL of Fetal Bovine Serum or Donor Bovine Serum (DBS) to each tube and gently swirl the tube to mix. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S01 -->
2. Release MuSCs from digested myofibers by quickly pipetting the digested fibers up and down 10 times with a 25 mL serological pipette. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S02 -->
3. Centrifuge tubes for 15 seconds at 400 × g at 4°C to sediment leftover debris. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S03 -->
4. Collect the supernatant from each tube and filter it through a 70 µm cell strainer placed in a new 50 mL tube labeled according to each mouse replicate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S04 -->
5. Centrifuge each tube at 400 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S05 -->
6. a. Remove supernatant and resuspend mono-nuclear cells in 0.5–1 mL of SM to count cells on a hemocytometer. b. Count ICs for the single-color/Fluorescent minus one (FMO) control samples at this step. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S06 -->
7. Note: If too many red blood cells are seen in the pellet, perform an Ammonium Chloride Potassium (ACK lysis) treatment to lyse them according to the manufacturer's protocol. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S07 -->
8. Note: If too many red blood cells are seen in the pellet, perform an Ammonium Chloride Po-
tassium (ACK lysis) treatment to lyse them according to the manufacturer’s protocol https:// www.thermoﬁsher.com/us/en/home/references/gibco-cell-culture-basics/cell-culture-protocols/ red-blood-cell-lysis-using-ack-lysing-buffer.html. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S08 -->

### Antibody staining of mono-nuclear cells associated with skeletal muscle

1. Label 5 mL FACS tubes for unstained, single-color controls (SSC), and fluorescence-minus-one (FMO) controls listed below: a. Unstained. b. SSC-Propidium Iodine (PI). c. SSC-Calcein Blue (CB). d. SSC-APC. e. SSC-APC-Cy7. f. SSC-PE-Cy7. g. FMO-APC. h. FMO-APC-Cy7. i. FMO-PE-Cy7. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S01 -->
2. Label FACS tubes for each experimental sample. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: Keep a ratio of 1×10^6 cells per 100 µL of SM. Antibodies have been carefully titrated to work optimally at this ratio. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S03 -->
3. Transfer 4×10^6 cells to their respective FACS tubes in a final volume of 400 µL of SM. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S04 -->
4. Stain cells in control and experimental samples with fluorescently conjugated antibodies according to the staining scheme to detect target antigens (Table 1). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S05 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Shield stained cells from light and keep tubes partially immersed in ice to prevent cells from internalizing antibodies. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S06 -->
5. Incubate stained cells on ice for 30 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S07 -->
6. Wash stained cells by adding 3 mL of SM to each FACS tube. Centrifuge at 360 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C. Decant the supernatant and resuspend in 400 µL of SM. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S08 -->
7. Incubate stained cells with PE-Cy7 Streptavidin antibody for 20 minutes and keep on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S09 -->
8. Wash stained cells by adding 3 mL of SM to each tube. Centrifuge at 360 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C. Remove the supernatant and repeat the wash step one additional time, for 2 washes in total. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S10 -->
9. Filter cells through a 40 µm cell strainer and into freshly labeled FACS tubes to prepare for FACS analysis. Keep stained cells in tubes immersed on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S11 -->

### 15 min prior to FACS analysis

1. 15 minutes prior to FACS analysis, filter cells through a 40 µm cell strainer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S01 -->
2. Add PI and Calcein Blue to corresponding tubes 15 minutes prior to FACS (Table 1). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S02 -->

### Flow cytometry and FACS-based puriﬁcation of MuSCs

1. Set up the BD FACS Aria III cytometer as specified by the manufacturer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T7-S01 -->
2. Use a 70 µm nozzle with a flow rate of 2.0–4.0. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T7-S02 -->
3. Run your unstained control to set the background voltage for each channel. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T7-S03 -->
4. Run each single-color control (SCC) sample and set voltage for positive cells and record events for the top 25% of expressing events for fluorophore compensations. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T7-S04 -->
5. After compensation for all channels, run FMO samples to assist with drawing negative gates for APC (CD45, CD11b, TER119, SCA1, CD31) and positive gates for APC-Cy7 (β1 Integrin) and PE-Cy7 (CXCR4) (Figure 5). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T7-S05 -->
6. Sort CD45-; CD11b-; TER119-; SCA1-; CD31-; β1 Integrin+; CXCR4+ MuSCs for further analysis. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T7-S06 -->

### next 48-72 h

1. Freshly sorted MuSCs will appear as small, rounded cells that divide over the next 48–72 hours as they exit quiescence. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T8-S01 -->

### 24 h prior to FACS

1. Pre-coat wells with coating media (See materials and equipment) for 24 hours prior to FACS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T9-S01 -->

### Freshly isolated MuSCs

1. Freshly isolated MuSCs can be sorted directly into pre-coated wells that contain GM. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T10-S01 -->
2. Supplement cultured MuSCs with daily addition of 5 ng/mL bFGF and incubate at 37°C with 5% CO2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T10-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Do not remove media completely within the first few days since MuSCs have low adherence in the first 48 hours after FACS isolation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T10-S03 -->

### 48-72 h

1. Fresh MuSCs FACS-isolated from uninjured muscle will start to divide in 48–72 hours. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T11-S01 -->

### After 3 days of culturing

1. After 3 days of culturing, remove 1/2 the volume of GM and replace 1/2 the volume with fresh GM. Repeat this procedure 3 times. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T12-S01 -->

### After 5 days of culturing

1. After 5 days of culturing, passage the progeny of MuSCs (i.e., myoblasts) onto new tissue culture plates by performing the following: [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T13-S01 -->
2. Detach MuSCs from plates by removing 1/2 the volume of GM and replacing it with an equal volume of warmed 5 mM EDTA. Incubate plates for 20 minutes at 37°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T13-S02 -->
3. Confirm that >90% of cells have been detached from the plate under a microscope and then use a pipette to wash the bottom of each plate to gently push cells into a cell suspension. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T13-S03 -->
4. Transfer the cell suspension to a labeled 15 mL conical tube and centrifuge at 360 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T13-S04 -->
5. Resuspend the resulting pellet in GM to count cells in the suspension. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T13-S05 -->
6. Seed cells at the appropriate density and continue culturing in GM. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T13-S06 -->
7. Supplement with daily additions of bFGF. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T13-S07 -->

### Differentiating MuSC-derived myoblasts into myotubes in culture

1. a. Seed MuSCs into pre-coated wells containing differentiation media (DM). We perform differentiation assays in 96-well plates and thus seed 8,000 cells into 96-wells containing DM and without bFGF. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T14-S01 -->
2. b. To differentiate myoblasts into fully formed myotubes, culture the cells in DM for 48–72 hours. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T14-S02 -->

### Total RNA Extraction from freshly sorted MuSCs

1. a. Prepare an RNase-free environment on the lab bench and label 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T15-S01 -->
2. b. Aliquot 500 µL of TRIzol LS (Invitrogen, Cat #10296010) into each tube prior to going to the FACS facility. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T15-S02 -->
3. c. Sort 1–50,000 MuSCs into 500 µL of TRIzol LS, immediately vortex tube(s), and then add 250 µL of TRIzol LS to bring volume to 750 µL. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T15-S03 -->
4. d. Incubate tubes with RNA/TRIzol for 5 minutes at 25°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T15-S04 -->
5. e. Store RNA in TRIzol LS at -80°C for up to 2–3 months. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T15-S05 -->
6. f. Perform extraction of RNA according to the manufacturer's protocol (TRIzol LS). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T15-S06 -->

### Immunoﬂuorescence staining of ﬁxed MuSCs

1. a. Remove 1/2 the volume of GM from each well. Add back the same volume with 8% paraformaldehyde (PFA) (4% PFA final concentration) and incubate MuSCs at RT for 20 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T16-S01 -->
2. b. Stop fixation by washing cells with Phosphate Buffered Saline (PBS) with 0.1% Tween 20 (PBST) 3 times for 5 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T16-S02 -->
3. c. Permeabilize cells with 0.3% Triton-X for 20 minutes at 25°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T16-S03 -->
4. d. Wash cells with PBST 3 times for 5 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T16-S04 -->
5. e. Add blocking buffer (5% Normal Goat Serum, 3% BSA, 0.3% Triton-X in PBS) for 2 hours at RT. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T16-S05 -->
6. f. Without washing, add primary antibody in blocking buffer to each well and incubate for 12 hours at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T16-S06 -->
7. g. Remove primary antibody solution and wash cells 4 times for 15 minutes with PBST at 25°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T16-S07 -->
8. h. Add secondary antibody in blocking buffer to wells and incubate for 1 hour at 25°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T16-S08 -->
9. i. Remove the secondary antibody from solution by washing cells with PBST 4 times for 15 minutes at 25°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T16-S09 -->
10. j. Add Hoechst stain (1 mg/mL Hoechst in PBS) to cells and incubate for 15 minutes at 25°C. Alternatively, you can add Hoechst into the third wash in step 53i. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T16-S10 -->
11. k. Remove Hoechst stain solution and wash cells with PBST for 5 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T16-S11 -->

### Transduction of MuSCs with Lentivirus

1. a. Titrate virus to determine the optimal density that gives maximal transduction and minimal toxicity (anywhere from 1:100–1:500) as determined by GFP fluorescence and/or antibiotic selection. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T17-S01 -->
2. b. Make virus in 293T cells, concentrate virus with PEG-it viral precipitation reagent (System Biosciences, Cat# LV810A-1), and then resuspend in GM supplemented with 25 mM HEPES. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T17-S02 -->
3. c. Sort 3,000 MuSCs into coated wells of a 96-well plate containing 200 µL of GM. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T17-S03 -->
4. d. In a viral-only Biohazard class II biosafety cabinet, prepare diluted lentiviral stock by diluting lentivirus solution with 8 mg/mL Polybrene (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat. TR-1003-G) at the empirically tested viral ratio. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T17-S04 -->
5. e. Remove 1/2 the volume of GM from each well and add back the same volume with diluted viral media to get the desired ratio. Carefully pipette each well 5 times with a P200 pipette and incubate the plate for 15 minutes at 37°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T17-S05 -->
6. f. Quickly parafilm plates shut to prevent spilling of virus while spinning cells and centrifuge at 930 × g plates for 90 minutes at 32°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T17-S06 -->
7. g. Wash out virus by removing 1/2 volume (100 µL) and replacing 1/2 volume (100 µL) with fresh GM 8 times. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T17-S07 -->
8. h. After the last wash, add bFGF to a final concentration of 5 ng/mL before returning to 37°C to each well daily. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T17-S08 -->

### 24 h prior to transplantation

1. a. Following your institution's IACUC protocol, 24 hours prior to transplantation, inject a chemical agent into the Tibialis Anterior (TA) muscle of mice to induce injury. Note: We readily use 25 µL of 10 mM cardiotoxin (CTX) or 50 µL of 1.2% Barium Chloride (BaCl2). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T18-S01 -->

### Transplantation of MuSCs into pre-injured mice

1. b. Sort MuSCs at desired numbers into 500 µL of staining media (SM) in Eppendorf tubes and keep on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T19-S01 -->
2. c. Pellet cells by spinning them down at 400 × g for 5 minutes, remove supernatant, and resuspend cells in 25 µL of saline. Note: When transplanting a low number of cells (less than 10K) you will likely not see a pellet. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T19-S02 -->
3. d. To prevent cells from sticking to the plastic walls of the syringe, pre-coat the BD Biosciences syringe with FBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T19-S03 -->
4. e. Using a 31-gauge insulin syringe, take in 25 µL of cells (in saline) into the syringe. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T19-S04 -->
5. f. Inject the needle at a 25° angle for a few cm, then reduce angle to 0° (parallel with the TA) for a few more cm such that the tip of the needle is the mid belly of the TA. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T19-S05 -->
6. g. Inject the entire volume and slowly remove the needle from the TA and dispose in a sharps bin. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T19-S06 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: Removing the needle too quickly leads to leakage of cell volume from TA, and thus, compromising your transplantation experiment. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T19-S07 -->

## References

- [1] Protocol for the isolation of mouse muscle stem cells using fluorescence-activated cell sorting — https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xpro.2023.102656
